name: Burkina Faso
headline: Burkina Faso: +5.3% growth in 2025, −0.5% inflation, debt 53% of GDP
sections: Burkina Faso is a $27.7 billion economy (2025), the world's 122nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +5.3% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $3,072 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 6.6% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose −0.5% in 2025, in deflation, down from 13.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.5% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 6.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 53% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 45% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.5% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +5.8% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 65% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 50% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 61.3 years (2024). Population: 24.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
